design:
Decision 1: a separate Checks meter; the wall-time bar is not changed. The wall bar answers 'what was the build doing at each moment' and must still add up to the build's wall time. Check time overlaps other work, so it needs its own meter. Changing the bar's precedence would only hide building time instead.

Decision 2: each check run records when it got its slot. Waiting is slot time minus queued time, and running is end minus slot time. This is one stored timestamp, not a second tally.

Decision 3: a run recorded before this change has no slot time. Its whole time counts as running, and its waiting time is unknown (null), never 0, following the tally's rule (work_tally.py:15-17).

Decision 4: the landing wait is read from records that already exist: the approval transition and the landing, per task.

Hazard: one migration adds a nullable column to task_check_runs. It needs no backfill, and rollback drops the column. The operator's :8000 Hub runs it on its next restart.

lifecycle: Exploring until the operator approves it. It builds after slice 1 has landed: both edit hub/hub/project_checks.py and hub/hub/landing_queue.py. Slice 1 changes how runs are judged and re-run, and this slice changes where a run takes its slot.
problem:
The card's wall-time bar (hub/hub/work_tally.py:751-850, WALL_PARTS at :52) gives each instant to the first part that applies: building, then reviewing, then checks. With three tasks building in parallel, check time is almost all hidden behind building. The tally already sums check-run seconds (checks.seconds, :481-494), but the card does not show that figure.

How long a run waited for one of the MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS = 2 check slots (project_checks.py:73) is held only in memory (_slot_waited, project_checks.py:1534-1539). A row's started_at is when it was queued, so waiting and running are summed together, and the split is lost when the Hub restarts. Task check runs take their slot in project_checks.py:1809; landing-batch runs take the same slot in landing_queue.py:1313 and :1833, and record no wait at all.

A timeout counts as an ordinary failure (checks.failed). Time from approval to landing on main, which reached 5 h 18 m for AWOAW-1 on 2026-11-05, appears nowhere on the card.

requirements.statement: Each check run, whether a task's or a landing batch's, records the time it got a check slot, and the record survives a Hub restart. A run that never got a slot (cancelled or superseded while waiting) records none.

requirements.rationale: AWOAW's 2 h of check runs showed as 17 min because the wall bar gives overlapping instants to building first.
requirements.statement: A build's check figures count every check run for the build's tasks, including landing-batch runs, for its full duration, whether or not building or reviewing happened at the same time. The figures are: time running, time waiting for a slot, number of runs, number passed, number failed, and number timed out. A run in which any check ended by its time limit is counted as timed out and not as failed.

A check run with no recorded slot time counts its whole duration as running. When every run of a build lacks a slot time, the build's waiting figure is unknown (null), not zero. When only some runs lack one, the figure covers the runs that have one, and the build reports how many runs had no slot time.

A build's figures include, over its tasks that have landed on main, the total and the longest time from a task's last approval to its landing. They also give the number of approved tasks still waiting to land, and the longest wait among those so far.

The build card shows a Checks meter with check running time and slot-waiting time as its parts, and its total. Beside it, the card shows the timed-out count and the landing wait (total, longest, and any still waiting). The wall-time bar is unchanged. An unknown figure reads as unknown, not as 0.

in_scope: Recording when a check run got its slot, for task runs and landing-batch runs
The tally's check figures for a build: running, waiting for a slot, timed out, and landing wait
A Checks meter on the build card showing them
non_goals: Changing the wall-time bar's parts or their precedence
Changing MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS or how slots are shared
The project view and Activity tab: they read the same tally rows, but showing the new figures there is not part of this slice
Backfilling slot times for runs recorded before the change
Splitting a landing batch's run across the several tasks it carries: it stays booked as the tally books it today

summary: The spec page's build card gets a Checks meter that counts every check run for the build's work, whether or not other work was going on at the same time. It splits that time into running and waiting for a check slot, counts timed-out runs on their own, and shows how long approved work waited to reach main. Today a build like AWOAW (2026-11-05) had about 2 h of check runs, but its card showed 17 minutes, because the wall-time bar gives each instant to building or reviewing before checks. This is slice 4 of 'Checks any project can use, judged against a known-failing list'.
